title: Change Healthcare — America's billing system goes dark

scenes.narration: [serious] One stolen password jammed American medicine bills for months.
Change Healthcare handles billions of health insurance payments every year. It is part of UnitedHealth Group.
In February 2024, criminals used a stolen password to log in. The door had no second lock, like a code sent to a phone.
Nine days later, they locked the company's files. Pharmacies struggled to give people medicine.
UnitedHealth paid 22 million dollars to the criminals. The twist? A partner said the gang kept all the money.
And the data still leaked. Almost 193 million people were affected.
Officials blamed the BlackCat gang. One missing lock hit millions.

facts.claim: ALPHV affiliates got into Change Healthcare on February 12, 2024 through a Citrix remote-access portal using illicitly obtained credentials; the portal had no multi-factor authentication; ransomware was deployed nine days later, on February 21
UnitedHealth CEO Andrew Witty told Congress hackers used compromised credentials on a server without multifactor authentication, and that UnitedHealth paid a $22 million ransom in bitcoin

Change Healthcare processes about 15 billion claim transactions; the attack disrupted care and claims processing for months; UnitedHealth's final count was 192.7 million affected individuals (July 31 letter)
An alleged ALPHV/BlackCat affiliate ('notchy') claimed the gang kept the $22 million ransom; ALPHV shut down its servers in early March 2024

The attack, carried out by BlackCat affiliates, kept thousands of pharmacies and hospitals from processing prescriptions; the U.S. State Department offers up to $10 million for information on ALPHV/BlackCat

seo.title: Change Healthcare Hack: One Login, No MFA, 193 Million People
